page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.80-320 is a general-purpose, ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by an Ampere Altra processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. The configuration provisions 80 dedicated physical cores mapping directly to 80 vCPUs with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 320.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for operating system disks and persistent data storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs present in the design. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the Ampere Altra architecture utilizes dedicated physical cores rather than simultaneous multithreading, it prevents resource contention across logical threads, delivering consistent per-core execution. From a resource density perspective, the ARM architecture provides high compute parallelism with efficient core scaling relative to traditional x86 server classes.

VM.Standard.A1.Flex.80-320 is suited for highly concurrent, scale-out workloads compiled for the arm64 instruction set architecture. Common deployments include container orchestration nodes, multi-threaded software build pipelines, web serving infrastructure, scalable API backends, and distributed data processing frameworks that benefit from 80 independent physical cores and 320.0 GB of system memory.
